title: La crisi dei cookie di ansa e l'accesso consentless
titles: LA CRISI DEI COOKIE DI ANSA E L'ACCESSO CONSENTLESS

occhiello: LA CRISI DEI COOKIE DI ANSA E L'ACCESSO CONSENTLESS
lead: Roma, 3 ottobre 2026. L'agenzia di stampa ANSA impone barriere di accesso e pop-up di profilazione per la lettura dei contenuti sportivi, offrendo un abbonamento Consentless annuale al costo di sedici euro e novantanove centesimi.
corpo1: Stando ai dati tecnici e alle informative pubblicate su ansa.it il tre ottobre duemilaventisei, la piattaforma digitale della principale agenzia giornalistica Italiana gestisce l'accesso alle notizie attraverso due strade distinte per conformarsi alle normative sulla Privacy. Gli utenti che rifiutano i Cookie di profilazione e tracciamento pubblicitario possono aderire all'abbonamento denominato Consentless al costo di sedici euro e novantanove centesimi l'anno, un Servizio che garantisce la lettura di tutti i titoli e di dieci contenuti ogni trenta giorni senza rinnovo automatico. La società prevede inoltre piani alternativi per la consultazione senza limiti, mentre chi sceglie di accettare i Cookie permette a settecentocinquanta terze parti selezionate di raccogliere dati personali per finalità di marketing e ricerche di mercato. Il Servizio di assistenza clienti, attivo dal lunedì al venerdì dalle ore nove alle ore diciotto e trenta e il sabato fino alle quattordici, gestisce le richieste tramite l'indirizzo email registerchiocciolaansa.it e il numero verde ottocento novantatré ottantotto ottantuno, offrendo supporto tecnico agli abbonati che esauriscono la quota mensile e ricevono l'avviso del blocco temporaneo.

Write only a new Corpo 2 (350-400 words). No repetition of Corpo 1. No invented facts. No questions. No moralism. Close with a net statement based on concrete facts. Use the persona of Davide Longo.

       Context:* ANSA is the main news agency in Italy. They are monetizing privacy.
       Longo's Perspective:* This isn't just about privacy; it's a business move. It's about the commodification of data. If you don't want to be a product (data for 750 third parties), you have to pay. This is a shift in the information economy.
       The "Sport" Angle (as requested by the persona):* Since I'm Davide Longo, I should view this through the lens of how information reaches the sports world. News agencies like ANSA are the backbone for sports desks, clubs, and agencies. If access is gated by privacy choices, the speed and quality of sports reporting change. It's a cost of doing business.

       Theme:* The economic shift from advertising-based models to subscription-based "privacy premiums."
       Analysis:* Discuss the trade-off between data value and direct revenue. The 750 third parties represent the "real" product. The €16.99 is a way to filter users who are "expensive" to track or who refuse to be tracked.
       The Business Mechanism:* This is a move to stabilize revenue in an era where cookie-based advertising is under pressure (GDPR/Privacy laws). It's a strategic pivot to capture a segment of the market that values digital sovereignty.
       Connection to the "Sottocopertine" title:* It's happening under the radar, behind the technicalities of GDPR compliance.

       Drafting phrases (internal monologue):* "Non è una questione di privacy, è una questione di bilancio." (It's not privacy, it's the balance sheet). "Il dato è l'asset." (Data is the asset). "ANSA sta trasformando l'utente in un cliente pagante invece che in un prodotto pubblicitario." (ANSA is turning the user into a paying customer instead of an advertising product).

       Constraint Check:*
        *   350-400 words? (Need to expand).
        *   No repetition of Corpo 1? (Avoid repeating the €16.99 or the 750 companies details unless adding context).
        *   No invented names? (Stick to ANSA's model).
        *   No questions? (Check).
        *   Closing: A net statement.

       Refining the Tone:* "Il modello è chiaro: la privacy non è più un diritto garantito dalla navigazione gratuita, ma un servizio premium da acquistare." (The model is clear: privacy is no longer a right guaranteed by free browsing, but a premium service to be purchased).

       Developing the Content:*
        The move by ANSA represents a structural shift in how information is monetized in Italy. For decades, the "free" news model was sustained by the massive sale of user profiles to third-party advertisers. By introducing the "Consentless" tier, the agency is effectively placing a price tag on the refusal to be tracked. This isn't just a technical adjustment to comply with privacy regulations; it's a strategic reorganization of their revenue streams.

        From a business standpoint, the 750 third parties mentioned in the technical documentation represent the real engine of the traditional model. For a news agency, a user who accepts cookies is an asset that can be auctioned in real-time bidding markets. A user who refuses is a cost—a consumer of bandwidth and editorial effort who provides no direct data-driven ROI. The €16.99 fee acts as a filter to recoup the lost potential revenue from these "non-trackable" users.

        In the sports sector, where the speed of information is a competitive advantage, this gatekeeping has implications for the professional ecosystem. Agencies, journalists, and even clubs rely on the instant flow of wires. If the cost of "clean" information rises, the barrier to entry for smaller media outlets or independent observers increases. This creates a tiered information market: those who can afford the data-free access and those who must trade their personal details to stay updated.

        The "sottocopertine" (under the cover) aspect refers to how this transition is being framed as a compliance measure rather than a direct monetization of privacy. While the public discourse focuses on GDPR and user rights, the balance sheet focuses on the conversion of "data-refusers" into "subscribers."

        If this model proves scalable, the precedent will force other major Italian publishers to move away from the advertising-only model, transforming the right to data protection into a tangible line item in the consumer's monthly budget.

       Word count check:* The draft looks to be around 360 words.
       Tone check:* Cynical, business-focused, no "scandal" without proof, no questions.
       Closing:* "If this model proves scalable... [Consequence]."

        Il passaggio verso questo modello di accesso non è una semplice manovra di adeguamento normativo, ma una riconfigurazione economica della gestione del dato. Nel
